title: “Last-Place Aversion”: Evidence and Redistributive Implications

original_source.version_note: Complete original abstract only; full body inaccessible through attempted publisher/author routes.

central_claims: Individuals avoid last place in experimental risk-taking and redistribution choices; near-bottom income positions can oppose redistributive policies that help those immediately below.

source_manifest.title: “Last-Place Aversion”: Evidence and Redistributive Implications
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether second-to-last participants are less likely to allocate money to the person below them; replication N=144, original focal N=42, p=.154. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

answers.rationale: No unambiguous later independent support for the stated central claim was established in the sources read.
The available evidence does not settle successful independent reproduction of the central claim.

The larger independently collected redistribution comparison did not retain the selected last-place-aversion result (N=144 versus 42, p=.154, opposite direction). Other risk-taking and public-policy claims were not tested by this comparison.
